sourceBasis.step: Add one private vertex adjacent to both ends of each edge of the Vertex Cover instance. A cover leaves a forest. Conversely, any feedback vertex set hits each edge triangle, so replacing any selected private vertex with an endpoint yields a cover of no larger size. A bag for each private vertex and its endpoints gives treewidth at most max(n−1, 2) for original order n, with polynomial encoding size.

sourceBasis.step: Logarithmic-pathwidth Feedback Vertex Set is XNLP-hard, so it is W[1]-hard. A graph’s treewidth is at most the width of the supplied path decomposition, which can be discarded. For a Clique input of order n and parameter k, the output treewidth is at most g(k)(1+log₂ n) for a computable g. Use the computable cutoff for a slope at most 1/g(k). Above the cutoff the exponential factor is polynomial in n, and below it the computable exponent has a finite maximum controlled by k. The polynomial-size reduction output then gives an FPT algorithm for Clique.
